To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a GPU-outsourcing mechanism to preserve privacy of all stakeholders during training and prediction; (2) we propose an efﬁciency-preserving mechanism to hide the weights of the model; (3) we propose a dynamic quantization mechanism that supports large changes in weight magnitude during training; (4) we propose a novel outsourcing mechanism that supports both training and prediction, and is efﬁcient in both pre-computation and on-demand computation.
we propose the ﬁrst private outsourcing solution for training and prediction of neural networks.
we propose Goten, a GPU-outsourcing trusted execution framework that supports private training and prediction of neural networks with dynamic quantization.

The main takeaway from our work is that
outsourcing training is possible by leveraging the GPU’s hardware features and the GPU’s ability to hide the computation results from the CPU.
outsourcing training to untrusted GPU is feasible, and it is possible to preserve privacy of both training and inference.
